Budget & Procurement · verification record

Spend Request, End to End

A purchase carried the whole way on a local copy of production: access granted, a budget built and approved, a supplier admitted, three requests raised, two purchase orders issued, received and settled, and one request stopped. Every screen below was captured live, in order, by five different people.

Run 23 September 2026Local dev server, prod-copy database56 screens, nothing staged

How this was run

Headed Chromium driving localhost:3113 against ea_sys_prod_local, with PROCUREMENT_MODULE_ENABLED=true. The database held the 41 chart-of-accounts categories and nothing else from the module: no budgets, no suppliers, no approval grants, no requests. Every figure, row and permission in these screens was created through the interface during the run.

Five throwaway local accounts were minted for it, because the separation this module enforces cannot be demonstrated by one person:

Sam Superadmin
Super admin. Grants procurement access to everyone else.
Rana Requester
PO Author. Runs the budget, raises requests, receives what arrives.
Amir Approver
PO Approver, ceiling AED 20,000.
Farah Final
PO Approver, unlimited. The final tier.
Sally Settle
Finance Settle. Vets suppliers, confirms receipt.

1

Who may do what

Nothing in this module is reachable by job title. Capability is granted per person from a catalogue of four roles, and the amount somebody may approve lives on the person rather than the role.

2

Building the budget

A budget belongs to one coded event and opens with a blank line per account-group category. Every category must end up with either a planned amount or an explicit not-applicable mark, so nothing is left unconsidered by accident.

3

The budget decision

Approval routing picks the lowest tier whose ceiling covers the amount and never offers a request back to the person who raised it. At AED 58,000 there was only one tier that qualified.

4

Admitting a supplier

Proposing a supplier and approving one are deliberately different hands. An order cannot be raised against a supplier nobody has vetted.

5

Raising the request

The request form answers the budget question as the requester types, so the check at submit confirms what was already on screen rather than springing a surprise.

6

Approval, and the order it becomes

A decision inside the approver's ceiling issues the purchase order in the same transaction. The ask and the commitment keep separate numbers.

7

Receiving

Receipt is recorded as everything or part of it. Below AED 50,000 one person closes it.

8

When it does not fit

An overspend is routed, not blocked. The approval bands are skipped entirely and the exception goes to the final approver alone.

9

Two people for the large one

At or above AED 50,000 a full receipt needs a second person, and the person who received it is not offered the confirmation.

10

Stopping a request

Two different endings: withdrawn back to draft and editable, or cancelled for good with a reason on the record.

What the run proves passed

  • Numbering. Requests came out PR-2026-0001 to PR-2026-0003 and orders PO-2026-0001 and PO-2026-0002, each in its own yearly sequence.
  • Routing skips a tier it does not fit. The AED 58,000 budget never appeared in Amir's queue, because his ceiling is 20,000. It went to Farah, the only tier that covered it. The AED 15,000 request went to Amir, as the lowest ceiling that covered it.
  • The requester is never the approver. Rana authored the budget and every request and was never offered a decision on any of them.
  • An overspend is routed, not blocked. AED 55,000 against a 40,000 line read OVER_BUDGET and went straight to the final approver, bypassing the bands, with the reason recorded on the trail.
  • The purchase order is issued in the decision transaction. Approving PR-2026-0001 produced PO-2026-0001 with no second step, and the request moved to CONVERTED.
  • Two people above AED 50,000. Rana marked PO-2026-0002 received and was given no way to confirm it. Sally, holding the confirm-receipt permission, was. Below the floor, PO-2026-0001 closed on one pair of hands.
  • The supplier gate holds. Rana could propose Gulf AV but had no Decide button; Sally did. An order waits on an unapproved supplier.
  • Pre-submit checks refuse early. A budget cannot be submitted until every category carries an amount or a not-applicable mark, and a request cannot be submitted without at least one quote. Both refused on screen with the reason, before anything was sent to anyone.
  • A received order cannot be cancelled. The order card said so in as many words once receipt was recorded.
  • The audit trail is written. 60 rows across EventBudget, BudgetLine, SpendRequest, Commitment, Supplier and ApprovalRequest by the end of the run.

Two things worth knowing observed

  • The purchase-order email is failure isolated, and it was proved by accident. PR-2026-0001 asked for the order to be emailed to the supplier on issue. SES rejected it, because the event's from-address is not a verified identity in this environment. The send failed, was logged at error, then logged again as procurement/commitments:auto-send-skipped with code SEND_FAILED at warn, and the approval and the purchase order still committed. The order simply reads "Sent to supplier: Not yet" with a Send button beside it. An email provider outage cannot cost you a purchase order. This is environment, not defect: on production the address is verified.
  • A super admin cannot be an approver. The procurement grants dialog is hidden for SUPER_ADMIN targets, and approval authority is read only from the two grant columns on the person, with no role arm anywhere in approvalCeilingAed or resolveApprover. So approval authority can only ever be given to an ADMIN, ORGANIZER or below. That reads as deliberate, and defensible: the platform owner is not the money approver. It is worth stating plainly, because on a fresh organisation whose only account is a super admin, nothing can be approved until somebody else is granted a ceiling.

What changed because of this run fixed

The screens above are the system as it was on 23 September 2026. Seven things the run turned up were fixed the same day, so a few of these captures now show older behaviour. See CHANGELOG.md for the detail.

  • An over-budget exception now needs a written reason. It did not, on an active budget: the requirement was the frozen budget's alone, so an unexplained overspend could reach the final approver. The justification in step 41 was volunteered, not demanded.
  • A rejection now carries its reason on every subject, matching what supplier rejections always demanded.
  • A receipt can be taken back while it is unconfirmed, audited, restoring the order's cancellable state. Marking received was the one irreversible click.
  • A failed purchase-order email is written down on the order and shown as a standing warning, rather than living only in the toast the approver saw once. The "Sent to supplier: Not yet" in step 37 is exactly the reading this fixes.
  • A draft budget can mark every remaining category not applicable in one go, and those lines now sort to the bottom rather than padding the table. Steps 13 and 14 were twelve separate round trips.
  • A sourcing method the quotes contradict is refused. Step 37 records "Single quote" on a request carrying two, which nothing objected to at the time.
  • The module's status badges moved onto the theme tokens, so the greys and the in-flight blue are the org's rather than raw palette colours.

What this run did not cover

Named so that nobody reads this document as more than it is:

  • Budget close-out and sign-off, and the reopen and unfreeze paths.
  • Changing an approved amount, which re-routes on the new total, and cancelling an issued order.
  • Partial receipt, as distinct from the full receipt shown here.
  • The 48 hour delegate and the 96 hour escalation, which are time based and belong to the worker tier.
  • Foreign currency, so no rate to AED was ever supplied or validated. Everything here is AED.
  • Supplier CSV import, the product catalogue, revenue and margin, and the QuickBooks connector.

One test-harness note

Two decision clicks appeared to do nothing on the first attempt. Both were the Next dev server compiling the decide route on first hit and taking longer than the script waited, not a product fault: the same clicks committed immediately once the wait was raised. Worth remembering if you script against npm run dev rather than a built server.
